items.text: Gloria Romero is a former state senator who served in the California Legislature from 1998 to 2010. She was the Senate Majority Leader, a position she held for three years as the first woman to do so. She taught as an adjunct professor at Pepperdine University and California State University, Los Angeles. In 2010, she wrote the state's "Parent Trigger" law, which allows parents to petition for change at poor-performing schools. She was a lifelong Democrat but registered as a Republican in 2024, saying the party had abandoned working families.

items.text: Romero supports school vouchers that let parents use public money for private school tuition, and she proposes cutting remedial coursework to help students finish degrees faster. She said she would push to cut administrative spending in higher education and proposed a policy requiring universities to offer the courses students need to graduate on time. She also supports restoring the SAT requirement for college admissions and Title IX protections for women in sports. Romero lists fighting antisemitism on college campuses among her top priorities and has criticized the Democratic Party's response to the issue.

items.text: She said she would work to reduce housing regulations to improve affordability. She proposes cutting the number of state commissions in half. She has said she wants the state to open public lands to new oil production. She has also said she wants to review the political leanings of faculty at state public universities.
